After breakfast, visit the Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe, one of the most important Catholic pilgrimage sites. According to tradition, the Virgin of Guadalupe appeared to Juan Diego in 1531, and her image appeared on his cloak.

You’ll visit the New Basilica and see Juan Diego’s cloak. The Old Basilica, built in 1700, is gradually sinking.

Continue to Teotihuacán, about 50 km north-east of Mexico City. The site is known for the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon. The city was founded in the early first century AD and reached its peak around AD 500, when its influence extended far beyond central Mexico.

After the tour, return to the hotel for the night.
Pyramid and stone platforms along a wide avenue in Teotihuacán, Mexico
Teotihuacán: ancient stepped structures and a pyramid against a mountain backdrop

After breakfast, depart for Cuernavaca, about an hour’s drive from Mexico City. Its mild climate has earned it the nickname ‘City of Eternal Spring’.

In Cuernavaca, the itinerary includes the Palace of Cortés, a colonial building associated with Hernán Cortés, and the 16th-century cathedral.

Continue to Taxco, a colonial mountain town in the state of Guerrero known for its silverwork. You’ll see Santa Prisca Church, one of Mexico’s notable Baroque churches, and the Zócalo, surrounded by colonial buildings, restaurants and silver shops.

You can also visit the silver mines and a market selling jewellery made by local artisans.

One night at Agua Escondida (3-star), in a standard room.
